subject: Architecture
title: The Truss Bridge: Triangles of Steel
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Truss Bridge: Triangles of Steel.

hook.text: A triangle is the only shape that can't be deformed without breaking a side. Truss bridges use hundreds.

buildup.text: Steel beams arranged in triangular patterns create a framework that is both light and incredibly strong.

discovery.text: Different truss patterns — Pratt, Warren, Howe — distribute forces in different ways for different loads.

twist.text: Railroads made truss bridges famous. Thousands were built across America in the 1800s from standard kits.

climax.text: The Forth Bridge in Scotland uses 54,000 tons of steel trusses — visible engineering as architecture.

punchline.text: A shape you learn in kindergarten holds up trains.

quiz.question: Why are triangles used in truss bridges?
options: They look more attractive than squares
Triangles cannot be deformed without breaking a side
They use less paint than curved structures
